summary: Bald Knob, Union County, IL: a 60-ft fire tower from 1930 (builder disputed) is gone; a 111-ft Bald Knob Cross of Peace (completed 1963) now stands on the summit.

facts.design: 60-foot steel lookout tower with a glass-enclosed lookout house (1930)
facts.status_note: Tower removed; a 111-foot cross with an observation platform now stands on the site

events.note: State Department of Conservation erected a 60-foot steel lookout near Bald Knob (newspaper account); a listing from about 1942 credits the U.S. Forest Service instead
First Easter sunrise service on Bald Knob; held annually since
Lighted electric cross, 70 feet high, mounted on the 60-foot tower for the Easter service
Plan for a 150-foot cross with a lookout post; the Forest Service agreed to dismantle the old fire tower on completion
111-foot cross completed (Wikipedia gives 1963); a 1974 article says it replaced a 40-foot neon cross mounted on a fire tower
Board disputes led to litigation; a court lock-down barred upkeep of the cross while proceedings continued

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1930 newspaper account says the State Department of Conservation erected the tower. A listing from about 1942 says the U.S. Forest Service erected a tower named Bald Knob Lookout Station. No source dates the handover, and the register names the Forest Service as administrator today, so the story reports both.
The 1953 plan called for a 150-foot cross. The cross built stands 111 feet, as Wikipedia and the 1974 article both describe.

sources.title: The Cross in the New Millennium (historical marker)

notes_for_editor: The 60-foot height in the brief (18.3 m) is supported by the 1930 newspaper account on the Forest Lookouts page, so it is kept. The builder is disputed (state in 1930, Forest Service in a c.1942 listing) and the story says so. Visitor access is not described in any source read, so the brief's access 'unknown' stays and no access fact is written. Not used: byway.world (rate-limited on fetch), everafterinthewoods.com and a PBS video (search snippets only), and a 1996 USGS/NGS survey designation 'BALD KNOB LOOKOUT TOWER' printed on the Forest Lookouts page, because a survey name does not show that a tower stood. The marker does not say when the cross restoration was finished; the story says so.
